6L/768d SP8192, alpha-uniform stratified t-sampling (T_MAX 0.5→0.6, loss /mask_prob), 8400s, 3058 steps — 0.003 BPB improvement over uniform-t (within noise). Low-t CE regressed significantly (t=0.05: 1.08→1.75, t=0.1: 1.46→1.86), mid-t improved slightly (t=0.3: 2.37→2.28), high-t unchanged. Variance-optimal sampler but low-t was already cheap to serve, so reallocation net break-even.

6L/768d SP8192 alpha-uniform, MLP 3x→4x (55M params), 8400s, 2935 steps — regressed 0.028 BPB. Low-t CE IMPROVED (t=0.05: 1.75→1.62, t=0.1: 1.86→1.66) but mid-t where BPB weight is highest got WORSE (t=0.3: 2.28→2.46). Extra FFN capacity absorbed by pattern-matching at easy noise levels; not enough steps to train wider net into its useful regime. Reverted.

6L/768d SP8192 alpha-uniform, partial self-conditioning (1/3 steps do detached teacher fwd, sc_emb = softmax(logits_pass1) @ embed.weight[:V] added to input emb at all positions with fixed gate=1.0, always-2-pass at eval), 8400s, 2719 steps (-11% from sc cost as predicted). +0.029 BPB regression. Per-t: sc HELPS high-t (t=0.9 7.15→7.07, t=0.7 ≈equal) and HURTS low-t (t=0.05 1.08→1.76, t=0.1 1.46→1.70) — the sketch hypothesis that sc_emb at unmasked positions would be "redundant but harmless" is wrong. At low-t unmasked positions the predicted emb is ≈ true emb but not exactly, and adding it actively pollutes the signal. ELBO weight (1/mask_prob) dominant at low-t so regression wins. Reverted. v2 candidate: mask-gated sc (sc_emb * mask.unsqueeze(-1)) would fix the unmask pollution.

6L/768d SP8192 alpha-uniform, Muon+ col_row post-polar normalization (arXiv 2602.21545, divide each col by L2 norm, then each row by L2 norm, after NS5). 8400s, 3050 steps (overhead negligible as predicted). +0.102 BPB regression. final_smooth_loss 0.47 vs baseline 0.74 — model fit training data much harder but generalization collapsed. Per-t: uniformly worse at low-mid t (t0.05 1.08→1.82, t0.3 2.37→2.66), ≈equal at high-t. Diagnosis: col_row makes u Frobenius = sqrt(fan_out) regardless of shape. Compounded with our rms_scaling sqrt(max(1, fan_out/fan_in)), tall matrices get over-scaled updates: fc (2304×768) ~1.73x, out_head (8192×768) ~3.27x. Paper avoids this by EXCLUDING lm_head from Muon (see exclusion list in MuonPlus.__init__). Our SplitOptimizer puts out_head.weight in matrix_params → huge over-scaled update per step → memorization. Reverted. Possible fixes before shelving: (1) try row_col instead (fat matrices over-scaled by sqrt(3) on proj only, out_head OK), (2) exclude out_head from Muon and put in Adam (matches paper recipe), (3) keep rms_scaling off when Muon+ active.

6L/768d SP8192 alpha-uniform, route out_head.weight from Muon→Adam (EMBED_LR 0.03), matching MuonPlus paper's lm_head exclusion. Optimizer buckets: Muon 37→36, Embed 2→3. 8400s, 3055 steps, final_smooth_loss 0.46. +0.0511 BPB regression. Per-t bimodal: t=0.05 dropped dramatically (1.7→0.92) but at mask_prob ~0.008 only ~4 masked tokens/seq — small-sample variance explains most/all of it. t=0.1 REGRESSED (~1.55→2.05) and t=0.2-0.3 slightly worse; t≥0.5 unchanged. Diagnosis: moving out_head to Adam also removed the rms_scaling sqrt(max(1,fan_out/fan_in))=3.27x LR multiplier it was getting under vanilla Muon. Adam@0.03 delivers per-element updates but total update magnitude on the 8192×768 matrix is much smaller than Muon+rms_scaling was producing. At this compute budget the vocab projection needs the larger updates. Kills the "unlock clean Muon+ retry" story: there is no clean out_head configuration that lets col_row help elsewhere without either over-scaling out_head (original Muon+ failure) or under-training it (this run). Reverted. Muon+ to parking lot.

6L/768d SP16384 (60.6M params: embed 12.58M + out_head 12.58M + bias 16K + stack 35.5M) alpha-uniform, vanilla Muon, no sc, 8400s on 2xRTX5080 (524K eff batch), 2791 steps (-9% vs baseline due to larger embed/out_head per-step cost). final_smooth_loss 0.486 (vs 0.47 baseline, expected higher for 16384-way classification). -0.0458 BPB over prior best 1.5556. Per-token CE uniformly higher at every measured t (t=0.05 1.08→1.46, t=0.3 2.28→2.65, t=0.7 5.70→5.89) but bytes-per-token increased more, net BPB win. Bits-saved check: t=0.05 went 9.01-1.08=7.93 (SP8192) to 9.70-1.46=8.24 (SP16384), so absolute information extracted per token went UP. Continuation of the clean SP1024→SP4096→SP8192→SP16384 curve. Artifact-fit caveat: model is now 60.6M params (vs 48M) — submission packer (external to repo) needs to get ~4x compression on an int8-quantized weights table; achievable with zstd but unverified end-to-end.

6L/768d SP16384 (60.6M) alpha-uniform + mask-gated partial sc v2 (1/3 steps run detached teacher fwd, sc_emb = chunked bf16 softmax(logits) @ embed.weight[:V], added to input emb at masked positions ONLY via mask gate), 8400s 2xRTX5080, 2494 steps (-11% from sc cost, matches sc v1 overhead). -0.0047 BPB over no-sc SP16384 baseline 1.5098 — small but real improvement, compounds sc v2 with SP16384. Per-t (vs no-sc baseline): t=0.1 2.31→2.01 (-0.30), t=0.2 2.32→2.14 (-0.18), t=0.5 4.31→4.22 (-0.09), t=0.3 2.65→2.84 (+0.19), t=0.05 1.46→2.19 (noisy, few masked tokens). Gating by mask killed v1's low-t pollution failure mode as hypothesized — v1 regressed 0.029 BPB because adding sc_emb to already-perfect unmasked embeds corrupted the signal; v2 only perturbs masked positions, where sc_emb is a reasonable prior. Keep.

6L/768d SP8192 (48M) alpha-uniform + sc v2 + Newton-Muon (arXiv 2604.01472; right-precondition Muon grad by K⁻¹ where K=EMA(ZᵀZ/N), β=0.9, γ=0.2, refresh k=16 steps, block-diag on fc_down, K_init=1e-3·I). 8400s 2xRTX5080, 2542 steps (~8% slower than NMUON=0 due to per-microbatch XᵀX hook fp32 matmuls). Per-t: t0.1=2.14 | t0.2=1.94 | t0.3=2.62 | t0.5=3.90 | t0.7=5.70 | t0.9=7.05 | final_smooth_loss 0.4832. Compare vs NMUON=0 sibling below: Newton-Muon wins -0.012 BPB at SP8192+sc v2 despite 200 fewer steps. Compare vs no-sc SP8192 baseline 1.5556: +0.012 regression, but that delta is entirely explained by sc v2 hurting at SP8192 (see sibling row). Impl notes: pre-hooks register on Muon-routed Linears only, guarded by torch.is_grad_enabled() to skip sc teacher fwd and eval; batch_ztz buffers pre-allocated in __init__ and in-place accumulated to prevent allocator fragmentation (OOM'd twice before this fix). Keep — test next at SP16384+sc v2 to see if it compounds with our best recipe.

6L/768d SP8192 (48M) alpha-uniform + sc v2 (mask-gated partial), vanilla Muon, NMUON=0. 8400s 2xRTX5080, 2736 steps. Per-t: t0.05=2.85 | t0.1=1.37 | t0.2=2.03 | t0.3=2.60 | t0.5=4.01 | t0.7=5.71 | t0.9=7.07 | final_smooth_loss 0.4636 (low-t very noisy; mid-t is the driver). Surprise finding: sc v2 REGRESSED +0.023 BPB vs no-sc SP8192 baseline (1.5556 row 103), opposite to what it did at SP16384 where it won -0.005. Hypothesis: sc_emb = softmax(logits) @ embed.weight[:V] gets more useful prior-mixing signal when embed is 16k×768 than 8k×768. sc v2 is vocab-dependent — keep it ONLY for SP16384 and above, not SP8192. This run also serves as the clean baseline vs Newton-Muon (sibling row above).

6L/768d SP16384 (60.6M) alpha-uniform + sc v2 + Newton-Muon (arXiv 2604.01472; K=EMA(ZᵀZ/N), β=0.9, γ=0.2, refresh k=16, block-diag on fc_down, K_init=1e-3·I). 8400s 2xRTX5080, 2331 steps (-7% vs NMUON=0 sibling at 2494 steps due to forward pre-hook fp32 matmul overhead on 37 Muon-routed Linears). Per-t: t0.05=1.77 | t0.1=1.75 | t0.2=2.31 | t0.3=2.89 | t0.5=4.22 | t0.7=5.99 | t0.9=7.27 | final_smooth_loss 0.4884. +0.0014 BPB vs SP16384+sc v2 no-NMuon (1.5051 row 109) — within run-to-run noise band. Mid-t (t=0.2 through 0.7) essentially unchanged; low-t swung 1.5-2.5 CE but only ~5 masked tokens/seq at those levels so dominated by small-sample variance. At SP8192 NMuon looked like a -0.012 win (vs NMUON=0 sibling) but that was within the same noise band once compounded with sc v2's vocab dependence. Net verdict: Newton-Muon is ≈neutral at our best recipe AND costs 7% throughput. Drop and move to parking lot. Code retained with NMUON=0 default so it's easy to revisit if another change makes it worthwhile (e.g., longer runs where the EMA warmup is cheaper to amortize).

6L/768d SP16384 (60.6M) alpha-uniform + sc v2 + SDPA attention + seq_len 512→1024. 8400s 2xRTX5080, 3364 steps — 35% MORE steps than seq=512 baseline at 2494 steps, despite seq=1024 being 4x the attention compute. SDPA (F.scaled_dot_product_attention) replaced manual `attn=(q@kᵀ)*scale; softmax; @v` path — the manual path was bandwidth-bound writing out the (B,H,T,T) score matrix, SDPA fuses into the memory-efficient kernel which is compute-bound on RTX 5080. First attempt at seq=1024 with manual attention OOM'd (9.6 GB attention activations across 6 layers at B=16 T=1024 H=12). Per-t: t0.05=1.99 | t0.1=2.09 | t0.2=2.21 | t0.3=2.68 | t0.5=4.11 | t0.7=6.01 | t0.9=7.34 | final_smooth_loss 0.4719. -0.0321 BPB vs prior best 1.5051 (row 109). Mid-t (t=0.3-0.5 where BPB weight is highest) uniformly improved: t=0.3 2.84→2.68, t=0.5 4.22→4.11. High-t and low-t essentially unchanged (within noise). CONFOUND: two changes bundled in this run — SDPA swap AND seq_len doubling. Numerically SDPA should be bit-close to the manual path (same math, same fp32 softmax accumulator under the hood), but the 35% step count increase suggests SDPA alone is already a big throughput win at seq=512. Need follow-up: seq=512 with SDPA to isolate how much of the -0.032 win is from extra context vs extra steps. Keep both changes regardless; this is the new leader.

6L/768d SP16384 (60.6M) alpha-uniform + sc v2 + SDPA + seq_len 512 (attribution run for prior row). 8400s 2xRTX5080, 3483 steps (3.4% more than seq=1024's 3364 — attention no longer bottleneck after SDPA so seq_len barely affects throughput). Per-t: t0.05=2.69 | t0.1=2.44 | t0.2=2.16 | t0.3=2.59 | t0.5=4.13 | t0.7=5.88 | t0.9=7.30 | final_smooth_loss 0.4726. ATTRIBUTION FINDING: seq=512 and seq=1024 are within 0.0001 BPB of each other — the entire 0.0321 BPB win vs prior 1.5051 baseline is from the SDPA attention swap alone. Seq_len 512→1024 does nothing for BPB at 8400s/524K-eff-batch. Mid-t slightly favors seq=512 (t=0.2 2.21→2.16, t=0.3 2.68→2.59, t=0.7 6.01→5.88), low-t favors seq=1024 but noisy. Keep seq=512 — frees VRAM for SP32768 and future wide-MLP/deeper tests. Seq_len move to rejected list. SDPA is pure upside and should have been in from day 1.

6L/768d SP32768 (85.8M: embed 25.2M + out_head 25.2M + stack 35.4M) alpha-uniform + sc v2 + SDPA. 8400s 2xRTX5080, 3051 steps (-12% vs SP16384 at 3483 due to embed/out_head bandwidth). Required BATCH_TOKENS=8192/gpu + GRAD_ACCUM=32 to fit VRAM (default 16384/16 OOM'd on cross-entropy's 2GB (B*T, V) logits tensor at V=32769). Per-t: t0.05=1.75 | t0.1=2.50 | t0.2=2.46 | t0.3=3.00 | t0.5=4.29 | t0.7=5.94 | t0.9=7.30 | final_smooth_loss 0.2454 (much lower than SP16384's 0.47 but not comparable — fewer bits/byte per token at bigger vocab). +0.0182 BPB vs SP16384 best 1.4731. Mid-t (where BPB weight is highest) uniformly regressed: t=0.2 2.16→2.46 (+0.30), t=0.3 2.59→3.00 (+0.41), t=0.5 4.13→4.29 (+0.16). Low/high-t basically unchanged. The SP vocab curve (SP1024→4096→8192→16384) saturated at 16384. At 10-min compute budget, SP32768's extra 25M params are under-trained — bigger vocab needs more steps to amortize, and we don't have them. Bonus penalty: artifact cap compression ratio goes from 3.8x (SP16384) to 5.3x (SP32768), tighter margin for no BPB gain. Reject. SP16384 is the keeper. Reconsider only if training budget gets substantially longer (6h+) or if a different change (deeper/wider model) alters the capacity-vs-steps trade.

6L/768d SP16384 MLP 3x→4x (67.7M: +7.1M FFN params) + sc v2 + SDPA + seq=512. 8400s 2xRTX5080, 3310 steps (-5% vs MLP 3x at 3483 from wider FFN bandwidth). Per-t: t0.05=1.88 | t0.1=2.13 | t0.2=2.39 | t0.3=2.57 | t0.5=4.03 | t0.7=5.89 | t0.9=7.27 | final_smooth_loss 0.4737 (matches MLP 3x at 0.4726 — same training-loss fit but val generalization slightly worse). +0.0056 BPB vs MLP 3x baseline 1.4731. Mid-t weakness unchanged (t=0.3 2.59→2.57 flat, the hypothesized capacity unlock didn't materialize). t=0.2 regressed (+0.23) while t=0.5 improved (-0.10). Retry of 4x MLP rejection from the SP8192 pre-SDPA era (which had regressed 0.028 BPB); SDPA throughput recovery narrowed the regression but didn't flip it. The capacity-vs-step tradeoff at 10-min budget still favors 3x. Revert. Move 4x MLP deeper into rejected list (now tested twice at different configs).

Accidental re-run of MLP 4x config (hightower hadn't synced the revert). 67.7M params, 3309 steps. Per-t: t0.05=2.31 | t0.1=2.02 | t0.2=2.34 | t0.3=2.66 | t0.5=4.06 | t0.7=5.93 | t0.9=7.18 | final_smooth_loss 0.4751. +0.0049 BPB vs MLP 3x baseline. Two MLP 4x runs within 0.0007 BPB of each other (1.4787 and 1.4780). RUN-TO-RUN NOISE CALIBRATION: variance band at 8400s/524K-eff-batch is very tight, ~±0.001 BPB. Previously "within noise" calls (Newton-Muon +0.001 at SP16384, seq=512 vs seq=1024 at 0.0001) confirmed as genuinely neutral.

8L/768d SP16384 (72.4M: +11.8M stack params from 6L→8L) + sc v2 + SDPA + seq=512 + MLP 3x. 8400s 2xRTX5080, 2805 steps (-19% vs 6L at 3483 due to sequential depth cost). Per-t: t0.05=2.43 | t0.1=1.86 | t0.2=2.36 | t0.3=2.60 | t0.5=4.12 | t0.7=5.88 | t0.9=7.22 | final_smooth_loss 0.4780 (WORSE than 6L's 0.4726 — under-trained deeper stack). +0.0147 BPB vs 6L baseline 1.4731. Same per-t pattern as MLP 4x: low-t improved (t=0.1 2.44→1.86), mid-t unchanged (t=0.3 2.59→2.60), high-t unchanged. FINDING: at 10-min budget we are STEP-STARVED, not capacity-starved. Three capacity experiments (MLP 4x x2, 8L x1) all regressed linearly with step count drop regardless of whether capacity went to width or depth. Extra params can't amortize in 10 minutes. Next levers must be per-step-value improvements (per-t loss targeting, Gauss-Legendre ELBO, LR tuning) rather than more params. Revert to 6L.
